capabilities.name: A law that covers AI agents is in force
capabilities.question: Is there a law in force in this country that applies to AI systems acting for users?

US.note: There is no federal AI law. Texas's Responsible AI Governance Act has applied since 1 January 2026, and other states have their own AI rules. Executive Order 14365 (December 2025) tells federal agencies to challenge state AI laws. These are binding AI rules, but they cover specific harms and uses, not agents acting for you, so it counts as limited.

evidence.title: HB 149, Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (bill history)
Executive Order 14365: Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence

GB.note: The UK has no AI law and no binding AI-specific rules, so it counts as none. Regulators apply general laws, such as the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 on automated decisions. In September 2026 Parliament's Joint Committee on Human Rights asked the government for a dedicated AI Bill; we found no government bill yet.

evidence.title: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025
Human Rights and the Regulation of AI (Fourth Report of Session 2026-27)
evidence.publisher: Joint Committee on Human Rights, UK Parliament

DE.note: The EU AI Act is in force in Germany, so it counts as live. Its transparency duties for AI systems apply since 2 August 2026. The Digital Omnibus (Regulation 2026/1744, in force 27 July 2026) delays the high-risk rules to December 2027 and August 2028, gives systems already on the market until 2 December 2026 to mark AI-generated content, and adds a new ban on AI built to make non-consensual intimate images or child sexual abuse material. The Act does not name shopping agents, but it covers AI systems that act for users.

evidence.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
AI Act: regulatory framework
EU Digital Omnibus on AI enters into force

IN.note: India has no AI law, and officials say none is planned; the India AI Governance Guidelines (November 2025) are voluntary. But binding IT Rules changes in force since 20 February 2026 make platforms label AI-made audio, images and video. Like the US rules, they cover specific harms, not agents acting for you, so it counts as limited.

evidence.title: MeitY unveils India AI Governance Guidelines
evidence.publisher: PIB, Ministry of Electronics and IT

evidence.title: India AI Governance Guidelines: Enabling Safe and Trusted AI Innovation
Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026 (G.S.R. 120(E))

BR.note: The Senate passed the AI framework bill (PL 2338/2023) in December 2024. In October 2026 it was still in a special committee of the Chamber of Deputies, waiting for the rapporteur's report, so it is not law. It passed one chamber, so it counts as announced. General laws such as the data protection law (LGPD) still apply.

evidence.title: Marco da Inteligência Artificial é aprovado em Plenário e vai à Câmara
PL 2338/2023 (ficha de tramitação)

MX.note: Mexico has no AI law and no binding AI rules. In October 2026 the Chamber of Deputies published a proposal to give Congress the power to legislate on AI, and we found no AI bill that has passed either chamber. As in Colombia, only lawmakers' proposals are pending, so it counts as none.

evidence.title: Gaceta Parlamentaria, 7 October 2026 (constitutional reform proposal on AI)

CL.note: The AI bill (boletín 16821-19) passed the Chamber of Deputies in October 2025 and is in its second step in the Senate. It sorts AI systems by risk and gives oversight to the data protection agency. It passed one chamber but is not law yet, so it counts as announced.

evidence.title: Proyecto de ley que regula los sistemas de inteligencia artificial (boletín 16821-19)
Ley de Inteligencia Artificial: últimas novedades en su tramitación

CO.note: Colombia has no AI law. The government's AI bill (043/2025 Senado, 324/2025 Cámara) was archived because it got no first vote within the session. Lawmakers filed a new AI bill (025/2026 Cámara) in July 2026, and it waits in committee. As in Mexico, only lawmakers' bills are pending, so it counts as none.

evidence.title: Colombia elige una inteligencia artificial centrada en la vida, los derechos y el interés público con radicación del proyecto de ley de IA
Proyecto de Ley 043/2025 Senado, 324/2025 Cámara (inteligencia artificial)
Gaceta del Congreso 878 de 2026 (Proyecto de Ley 025 de 2026 Cámara)

ES.note: The EU AI Act is in force in Spain, so the cell is live; its transparency duties apply since 2 August 2026, and the Digital Omnibus delays high-risk rules to December 2027 and August 2028. Spain already has an AI supervisor (AESIA), and on 26 May 2026 the government sent a bill to parliament to adapt the Act and give AESIA power to fine; we could not confirm whether it has passed.

evidence.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
El Gobierno aprueba el proyecto de ley que garantizará una supervisión humana y un uso confiable de la IA
evidence.publisher: Ministerio para la Transformación Digital y de la Función Pública

FR.note: The EU AI Act is in force in France, so the cell is live. Its transparency duties for AI systems apply since 2 August 2026, and the Digital Omnibus (Regulation 2026/1744) delays the high-risk rules to December 2027 and August 2028. The Act does not name shopping agents, but it covers AI systems that act for users.

evidence.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
AI Act: regulatory framework

CA.note: Canada has no AI law: AIDA died with Bill C-27 in January 2025. Bill C-36, the Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data Act tabled in June 2026, is a privacy bill that has not passed, and in September 2026 the AI minister would not commit to an AI bill.

evidence.title: C-36: Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data Act (LEGISinfo)
AI minister says system deployment needs regulation but no details yet

JP.note: The AI Promotion Act (人工知能関連技術の研究開発及び活用の推進に関する法律) has been fully in force since 1 September 2025, and the first AI Basic Plan under it was adopted in December 2025. It is a promotion law: it sets up the AI Strategy Headquarters and asks businesses to cooperate, with no penalties and nothing on agents acting for you, so the cell is limited.

evidence.title: AI法 全面施行 -次なるフェーズへ-
人工知能基本計画 (資料)

AU.note: Australia has no AI law. The National AI Plan (December 2025) dropped the proposed mandatory guardrails and ruled out a standalone AI Act, relying on existing privacy, consumer and other laws.

evidence.title: Australia introduces a national AI plan: four things leaders need to know
Mandatory AI guardrails put on hold with the release of national plan

NG.note: Nigeria has no AI law in force; the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 covers automated decisions as a general law. The government-backed National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill would apply to "AI agents" and sort AI systems into risk groups; in July 2026 the Senate ICT committee chair said it was going through third reading and would reach the president within weeks, but we found no report of final passage or assent.

evidence.title: 'National Digital Economy and e-Governance Act 2026 Ready in Weeks'
Nigeria Set to Pass Sweeping AI Rules for Digital Economy

KR.note: South Korea's AI Basic Act (the Framework Act on AI Development and Trust) took effect on 22 January 2026. It covers AI systems in general and requires notice to users before they use high-impact or generative AI, and it does not single out agents that act for users.

evidence.title: AI Basic Act takes effect on 22 January, per the Ministry of Science and ICT
Framework Act on the Development of AI and Establishment of Trust (AI Basic Act)

SG.note: Singapore has no AI law that covers agents acting for users. The IMDA's Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI, announced on 22 January 2026, is guidance, not law.

evidence.title: Singapore launches new Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI

ID.note: Indonesia has no AI law in force. The government's AI rules are still drafts: a presidential regulation on AI ethics dated 27 January 2026 was still a draft in June 2026, and the national AI roadmap was in public consultation in August 2025. We could not open the 2022 data protection law, which may cover automated decisions in general, so confidence is low.

evidence.title: Draft presidential regulation on AI ethics (dated 27 January 2026)
Komdigi opens public consultation on the national AI roadmap white paper

IT.note: The EU AI Act applies in Italy, and its transparency duties for AI systems have applied since 2 August 2026. Italy also has its own AI law, Law 132/2025, in force since 10 October 2025, which works alongside the Act. Its main chapters cover public administration, professions, courts and crime, and our sources did not name AI agents acting for users.

evidence.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
AI regulatory framework
Legge 23 settembre 2025, n. 132, Disposizioni e deleghe al Governo in materia di intelligenza artificiale

NL.note: The EU AI Act is in force in the Netherlands, so the cell is live. Most of it has applied since 2 August 2026, and the high-risk rules were pushed back to December 2027 and August 2028.

evidence.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
AI Act application timeline

capabilities.name: You can get your money back when an agent buys the wrong thing
capabilities.question: Do consumer or payment rules, or a regulator statement, clearly cover purchases or payments an AI agent made for you?

US.note: US rules refund unauthorized card and bank-account payments and billing errors, and card networks handle disputes, but they were written for human buyers. Authorization is defined as the consumer's permission, so an agent's mistake is a gray area. In April 2026 American Express announced protection for purchases made by registered agents, as a company product, not a rule.

evidence.title: Electronic Fund Transfers, Regulation E, section 1005.6 (liability of consumer)
American Express Debuts Agentic Commerce Experiences (ACE) Developer Kit and Announces Industry-First Protection for Registered Agent Purchases

GB.note: The Payment Services Regulations 2017 oblige banks to refund unauthorized payments, and section 75 of the Consumer Credit Act makes card lenders liable for faulty goods. Neither says what happens when software buys for you. HM Treasury's July 2026 consultation asks whether consent and liability rules for agent payments need changing; its answer is still open.

evidence.title: Payment Services Regulations 2017, regulation 76 (refunds for unauthorised payments)
Consumer Credit Act 1974, section 75
Modernising Payment Services Regulation (consultation)

DE.note: German law (BGB section 675u) makes the bank refund payments you did not authorize, and section 355 gives a 14-day right to withdraw from online purchases, whoever placed the order. Neither rule mentions agents. The EU's new payment rules (PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation), agreed in November 2025 and not yet applying, add stronger fraud refunds, but the Council's summary of the deal does not mention agents either.

evidence.title: BGB § 675u (Haftung des Zahlungsdienstleisters für nicht autorisierte Zahlungsvorgänge)
BGB § 355 (Widerrufsrecht bei Verbraucherverträgen)
Payment services: Council and Parliament agree to step up the fight against fraud and increase transparency

IN.note: The Reserve Bank of India's 2017 circular limits your loss on unauthorized electronic payments and orders banks to credit the money within 10 working days. The E-Commerce Rules 2020 require platforms to answer complaints within a month. Neither names agents, and an order an agent places for you may count as authorized.

evidence.title: Customer Protection: Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020

BR.note: Brazil's consumer code gives seven days to withdraw from a distance purchase, and the central bank's Pix refund scheme (MED) returns money after fraud or a bank error. The central bank says MED does not cover a purchase that went wrong, such as the wrong item, and no rule names agents.

evidence.title: Guia de implementação dos procedimentos de devolução no Pix (MED)
Lei 8.078/1990, Código de Defesa do Consumidor

MX.note: Condusef, the national commission that protects users of financial services, says a bank must credit a charge you do not recognize within about 48 hours while it investigates for up to 45 days, and for online buys the bank must prove it used online authentication. The consumer protection law (LFPC) covers online sales. None of it names agents, and an agent's order is one you asked for.

evidence.title: Cargos no reconocidos
Garantía y compras en línea

CL.note: Chile's consumer law (Ley 19.496), which SERNAC enforces, gives a right to withdraw from purchases made online, and Ley 20.009 makes the card issuer refund charges you say you did not authorize. Neither names agents, and an order an agent places for you may count as authorized.

evidence.title: Ley 19.496, normas sobre protección de los derechos de los consumidores
Ley 20.009, limita la responsabilidad de los usuarios de tarjetas de pago y transacciones electrónicas

CO.note: Article 51 of Colombia's consumer statute (Ley 1480) lets you ask for a payment reversal on online purchases that were fraudulent, not requested by you, not delivered or not as ordered, if you complain within five business days. It is the closest rule to this question anywhere in the eight countries, but it does not name agents.

evidence.title: Ley 1480 de 2011, Estatuto del Consumidor, artículo 51 (reversión del pago)

ES.note: Spanish law (Real Decreto-ley 19/2018, article 45) makes the bank refund payments you did not authorize, and the consumer law gives a 14-day right to withdraw from online purchases. Neither mentions agents. The EU's new payment rules (PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation), agreed in November 2025, are not yet applying and do not mention agents either.

evidence.title: Real Decreto-ley 19/2018, de servicios de pago (PSD2 in Spain: payment initiation and account information services; article 45 refunds unauthorised payments)
Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2007, Ley General para la Defensa de los Consumidores y Usuarios (article 102: 14-day right of withdrawal)
Payment services: Council and Parliament agree to step up the fight against fraud and increase transparency

FR.note: Article L133-18 of the Code monétaire et financier makes the bank refund payments you did not authorize, and French consumer law gives a 14-day right to withdraw from online purchases, whoever placed the order. Neither rule mentions agents. The EU's new payment rules (PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation), agreed in November 2025 and not yet applying, do not mention agents either.

evidence.title: Article L133-18 du Code monétaire et financier
Payment services: Council and Parliament agree to step up the fight against fraud and increase transparency

CA.note: The Bank Act caps your loss on unauthorized credit card use at $50, card networks' zero-liability policies go further, and the debit card code covers losses beyond your control; Interac e-Transfers have no legal limit. None of these rules or FCAC statements mentions purchases an AI agent makes for you.

evidence.title: Fraud and FCAC oversight of unauthorized transactions (briefing, Standing Committee on Finance)
Moving together: a systemwide response to financial fraud

JP.note: Japanese law refunds some unauthorized bank withdrawals and lets you cancel an online contract made by a clear input mistake, and card issuers cover fraud under their member terms, but none of these mentions agents. The Cabinet Office's Consumer Commission set up an expert panel on AI and consumer problems in 2026, which discussed spending limits, approval before purchase and cancelling agent actions, but it has not issued rules.

evidence.title: 第6回 人工知能(AI)技術の利用と消費者問題に関する専門調査会 議事録
evidence.publisher: Consumer Commission, Cabinet Office (消費者委員会)

evidence.title: 内閣府 消費者委員会 専門調査会にAICX協会代表理事 小栗 伸が登壇｜AIエージェント時代の消費者保護に向け、ガイドライン整備と人材育成の重要性を提言

AU.note: ASIC's ePayments Code sets who pays for unauthorised transactions, but it is voluntary and does not mention agents; Treasury's payments reform would let the minister make it mandatory. No rule or regulator statement covers purchases an AI agent made for you.

evidence.title: ePayments Code

NG.note: The CBN's Consumer Protection Regulations (2019) and its Consumer Protection Framework make banks refund fraud losses and unauthorized debits, with interest, unless the customer was negligent. None of these rules names AI agents, and an agent's order is one you asked for.

evidence.title: CBN Consumer Protection Regulations
Consumer Protection Framework

KR.note: The Electronic Financial Transactions Act is the main payment rule that comes up, but legal commentary says it assumes a person gives each payment instruction. It is unclear who pays when an AI agent buys the wrong thing, and no regulator position on agent purchases has been reported.

evidence.title: AI agent payments: the legal issues
Who pays when an AI agent buys the wrong thing

SG.note: MAS's E-Payments User Protection Guidelines decide who bears losses from unauthorised payments on bank and e-money accounts held by individuals and sole proprietors. Card payments fall under the Association of Banks in Singapore's card code instead. The guidelines do not mention AI agents, so it is unclear whether a purchase an agent made counts as one the person consented to.

evidence.title: E-Payments User Protection Guidelines (effective 16 December 2024)
E-Payments User Protection Guidelines

ID.note: We found no consumer or payment rule that clearly covers purchases an AI agent makes for you, and no regulator statement on agent purchases. We could not open the consumer protection law or Bank Indonesia's payment rules, so confidence is low.

IT.note: Italy applies the EU payment rules (PSD2), which require the bank to refund unauthorised payments right away. A payment counts as authorised only when the payer has consented. EU consumer rules also give a 14-day right to withdraw from online purchases. None of these names an AI agent, so it is unclear whether an order an agent places counts as the customer's consent.

evidence.title: Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2), Articles 64 and 73
Directive 2011/83/EU on consumer rights, Article 9
Decreto legislativo 27 gennaio 2010, n. 11 (payment services)
Codice del consumo, Decreto legislativo 6 settembre 2005, n. 206

NL.note: EU payment law, carried into Dutch law, makes your bank refund a payment you did not authorise, right away and no later than the end of the next business day after it learns of the payment, unless it suspects fraud. The rule does not say whether an order an agent places counts as authorised, and we found no Dutch rule or regulator statement that covers agent purchases.

evidence.title: Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2), Article 73: payment service provider's liability for unauthorised payment transactions
